Data Objects for Multiple Linear Regression Models

Source: R/mlm_data.R
mlm_data.Rd

Methods for preparing and working with data sets for fitting multiple linear regression (MLM) models. MLM data sets are implemented in a modular (“object-oriented”) interface, which allows for different types of MLM data (see ‘Details’ for a general specification of MLM data classes).

Usage

prepare_mlm_full_data(X, y, standardize = FALSE)

prepare_mlm_summary_data(z, R, bhat, sehat, n, var_y, df.residual = n - 2)

# S3 method for class 'mlm_full_data'
sample.names(dat, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mlm_full_data'
variable.names(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mlm_summary_data'
variable.names(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mlm_full_data'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mlm_summary_data'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary_mlm_full_data'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary_mlm_summary_data'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mlm_full_data'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mlm_summary_data'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

X

An n x J matrix containing observations about J candidate explanatory variables.

y

A vector of regression outcomes.

standardize

If standardize = TRUE, columns of X are standardized. If variables are in the same units already, you might not wish to standardize. Coefficients are always returned on the original scale.

z

A vector of z-scores (not yet implemented).

R

A J x J correlation matrix.

bhat

A vector of length J containing least-squares estimates of the coefficients (e.g., estimated using lm).

sehat

A vector of length J containing the standard errors of the least-squares estimates.

n

The number of samples.

var_y

This should be equal to sum(y^2)/(n-1). If y has a mean of zero, this should be the same as var(y).

df.residual

The residual degrees of freedom from estimation of the coefficients, e.g., using lm.

dat

An object of class ‘mlm_data’.

...

Other arguments.

object

An object of class ‘mlm_data’.

x

An object of class ‘mlm_data’.

Value

An ‘mlm_data’ object. It is a list with the following elements (and possbly others):

n

The number of samples.

nvar

The number of variables.

var_y

This is var_y = sum(y^2)/(n-1). It will be equal to var(y) if y is centered (i.e., has a mean of zero).

ss

An ‘ser_data’ object giving summary statistics derived from the MLM data (summary statistics are obtained under the assumption that the residual variance is 1). See prepare_ser_data for details.

xs

Scaling factors applied to the variables (e.g., columns of X). If no scaling is applied, this should be a vector of ones.

Details

Design of MLM data classes.

An MLM data object defines a data set for J candidate explanatory variables measured in n samples and a response variable or regression outcome. The canonical representation of MLM data is an n x J matrix X (containing measurements of the candidate explanatory ariables and a vector y of length n (containing measurements of the response variable). This canonical representation is generated by prepare_mlm_full_data. Other representations of MLM data are defined as MLM data classes.

An “MLM data” class has at a minimum the following elements:

  1. A function that creates the MLM data object (e.g., prepare_mlm_full_data). It should return an object of class ‘mlm_data’.

  2. A ‘sample.names’ method that returns the sample names.

  3. A ‘variable.names’ method that returns the variable names.

  4. Print and summary methods that output a summary of the data.

  5. A compute_XtXb method that returns the matrix-vector product drop(crossprod(X) %*% b) for a vector b of length J.
